claims.text: The intervention is addition of approximately 3 atomic percent chromium to a chromium-free refractory high-entropy alloy baseline.
Vacuum arc melting will produce a homogeneous distribution of chromium in the alloy.
Chromium atoms will be incorporated uniformly into the alloy matrix.
The chromium addition may form minor precipitates.
Chromium addition will enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Chromium addition will provide solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening and improved oxidation resistance will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Solid-solution strengthening and improved oxidation resistance will improve high-temperature creep resistance.
The chromium-modified alloy will retain microstructural characteristics comparable to those of the baseline alloy.
Comparable microstructural characteristics will preserve room-temperature mechanical performance.
Adding approximately 3 atomic percent chromium will not significantly increase the alloy's density.
At approximately 900°C under tensile loading, the chromium-modified alloy will have significantly greater yield strength than the chromium-free baseline.
The chromium-modified alloy will have no statistically significant change in room-temperature yield strength relative to the baseline.
The predicted effects apply when baseline and modified alloys are processed under identical vacuum arc melting conditions.
Changes in processing conditions may alter the effect of chromium addition.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on chromium concentration, processing parameters, and interactions between chromium and the other alloying elements.
